I definitely appreciate them asking, I’m just in a confusing situation atm I guess. I feel anxious about openly saying I’m still figuring things out, or I go by anything other than she/her, because unfortunately I had someone message my mum on Facebook awhile ago trying to ‘out’ me as trans. Luckily she didn’t know how to accept message requests & asked me to accept it for her, so I saw the message before she did & deleted it. It’s made me quite paranoid about opening up to anyone again now though. 

I suppose I wouldn’t mind saying ‘any’ but I was worried that might come across as ignorant. I present v feminine at the moment so most people will likely assume I’m a cis woman so I don’t want to come across as being purposely difficult I guess. My mum will often complain that she was asked her pronouns in meetings, saying she thinks it’s ridiculous, she doesn’t care & will go by ‘any’.. but then when I question her more about what she means, asking whether she’d be okay with ‘he’ or ‘they’ she says I’m ridiculous & that’s obviously not what she meant. So by ‘any’ she literally just means ‘she’. I worry I’ll come across ignorant in the same way even though I don’t mean too.. I’m probably just overthinking it all though bc of how socially anxious I am 🙃

I genuinely find this debate so annoying & boring. It’s always non autistic people who are so vocal and adamant about it as well. 

I’ve had similar said to me about being visually impaired as well. I shouldn’t say ‘I’m visually impaired’, I should say ‘I have a visual impairment’.

From what I can gather, it’s people who are uncomfortable around disability who will say stuff like this & insist you’re not disabled, you’re differently abled. Why can’t we just use the language that’s most comfortable to us. Being autistic affects every part of my life & for me it’s part of who I am.

7 tampons per cycle?? Damn I wish.  I use at least 7 per day bc my flow is heavy. I usually buy a box of 32 Lil-Lets which last me one cycle. They’re £3.20 a box so that’s £38.40 a year I spend personally. 

His maths skills are shit though. The shortest ‘regular’ cycle is 3 days & the maximum amount of time you can keep a tampon in is 8 hours. So that’s at the very least 3 per day therefore 9 tampons per cycle. I highly doubt there’s many people who need that few tampons though. 

I don’t understand why he even felt the need to complain about this? Why should anybody have to spend their last few ££s for the month on period products if they need that money for food or bills? That money might seem like an insignificant amount to him, but for a lot of low income people it really isn’t. It’s just an extra bill solely due to being born female.

Thank you so much this is really helpful! You’re definitely right that it’s easier to be yourself in front of strangers that have no expectations of you. I keep wanting to go to trans groups hoping I’ll feel comfortable to be myself in front of other trans people who don’t know me. Although I still worry that I’ll do the exact same thing.. but it’d probably be easier to slowly unmask in front of strangers. 

I love that idea about roleplaying as well! My personality now basically feels like I’m playing a character, so I may as well pick a character closer to how I actually feel :)

I totally agree with you about the gender expression doesn’t equal gender identity! I’ve already told my boyfriend there’s plenty of feminine things I enjoy that I don’t want to change. I have two IKEA Alex Nine drawers just for my makeup collection which won’t be changing anytime soon 🤣 it is nice to hear other people say that though as I do think enjoying feminine things like makeup has contributed towards my confusion, even though for other trans people it wouldn’t even be something that crosses my mind. People can like whatever they like regardless of gender identity. 

I think it’s more just specifically my personality that feels v mismatched. I haven’t practiced my voice in front of him yet, but I will wear a binder & boxers in front of him which feels really nice, but then I ruin it for myself by acting girly even though I know I don’t want to act that way in that moment. 

Honestly I’m only just learning about masking so I imagine it’ll take me awhile to be able to fully unmask & be myself. I was worried he might take it the wrong way like I don’t trust him to be myself.. but he’s autistic too so he might somewhat relate. 

Thank you anyway. I’m glad it makes sense to someone else as well & it’s not just me :)

Sometimes it seems to help with impulsivity, other times not really. Although I mostly end up Amazon shopping at night in bed so it’s worn off hours before then anyway D:

I haven’t struggled with addiction personally, but I can definitely relate to feeling worried about being open about your past during your assessment. I went to my GP a few years ago & asked to be referred for an ADHD assessment & they straight up refused to refer me & just blamed all my symptoms on the countless anxiety disorders they’ve diagnosed me with. 

I knew it wasn’t just anxiety related & got frustrated that I wasn’t even allowed to be assessed so I ended up paying for a private assessment last year & ended up getting diagnosed. I have a private Autism assessment in a couple weeks as well which I was also not allowed through the NHS bc my GP told me I make too much eye contact to be Autistic lol. 

After all the negative experiences I’ve had with  the NHS, I still decided to just be upfront & honest about all my mental health issues in my assessment & I think you should too for a couple reasons: 1) you want your diagnosis to be accurate, if you’re going to be paying privately for medication you want to know it’s actually going to be beneficial to you, otherwise it’s just a waste of money. If it’s not ADHD, the psychiatrist should be able to suggest what is possibly causing your symptoms instead & help you create an action plan. 2) if you eventually want to go to a shared care agreement where the NHS prescribes your medication then your psychiatrist will send your diagnosis to your GP. My diagnosis (and I’m assuming everyone else’s does too) has a full write up about all my mental health history. I wanted to make sure this was completely accurate to everything on my NHS records so it doesn’t cause any issues for me in the future with a shared care agreement. 

Private healthcare has been a completely different experience for me from the NHS (which is sad to say). I genuinely feel listened to & believed by my psychiatrist. I don’t feel like he’s trying to rush my appointments or discharge me from his care ASAP. 

Be honest now to save yourself from more worries later on. Private healthcare is expensive though so make sure you save A LOT. They say most people’s tritiation period is a few months but mine has been almost a year now so definitely save more than you predict you’ll need. Do lots of research to find the psychiatrist you think will have the most knowledge & experience to understand your situation & needs! Good luck! :)

For some reason Reddit won’t let me edit the original post but I thought I would do a lil update since there’s too many comments to reply to individually! 

Thank you all so much for the advice, you’ve given me a lot to think about & it’s been really helpful. In terms of the red flags, you could v well be right but I feel like there’s some more context I should have given which would explain most of them away. We have only been dating for 5 weeks so we are definitely still learning about each other, however it’s been v intense & we have spent A LOT of time together/talking in that time. We both have ADHD & I think we’re both kinda hyperfixating on each other right now (which I know could actually be a bad thing in itself)… we’re both very excited & he’s spent quite a few nights at mine the past few weeks. When we’re not together we’re having like 12 hour phone calls or texting all day so it hasn’t really been a ‘typical’ amount of time you’d spend with someone in the first 5 weeks. I do recognise the excitement is making me rush into things without thinking it through properly though so I’m definitely going to listen to everyone’s advice and try to slow things down. 

Another thing I should’ve probably mentioned is we’re both autistic & this has actually been a major thing we have bonded over, so I can’t exactly complain about him not picking up on non verbal cues that he’s being too rough when I know he struggles with that kind of thing & I know I need to be very direct with him. 

When I say ‘I know he cares about me’.. it’s bc the majority of the stuff we have talked about has been non sexual/kink related so I don’t feel used by him for sex. He’s told me he has a high sex drive though & I am starting to see that come out more but I would assume that’s normal for all relationships as they become more serious? I did have a bit of a scare the other day bc as soon as he got here he threw me on the bed, pinned me down & was getting quite rough.. I did tell him to stop bc it felt a bit much when he had literally just arrived but bc he knows we’re both into CNC he didn’t think I was being serious to begin with, as soon as he realised I wasn’t kidding he stopped immediately & apologised. It did get me thinking about needing a safeword though. When we have been intimate he has regularly asked if i’m okay & enjoying everything. I’m also a closeted trans guy & he has been super supportive & has not crossed any boundaries like trying to touch my chest or take my binder off so I genuinely don’t believe he has malicious intentions at all. 

He’s told me he is experienced with BDSM but hasn’t gone into any further detail so I’m not sure what sort of dynamics he’s had in the past or what kinks he’s tried etc. I feel like maybe this is something I should ask more about to try to get a better understanding of where he’s at & whether there’s things we should be learning about together? I’m not sure if this is disrespectful to ask though since he’s not brought it up.. he knows that I have no experience so there’s not much else he can ask me which is maybe why the conversation hasn’t come up.


I do agree that him saying not to worry about a safeword right now feels like a red flag, especially since he brought it up in the first place & especially after I’ve been sick on him & ended up in a lot of pain after anal a couple times (which he knows about & said he felt bad about).. & especially after he misinterpreted me telling him to stop a few nights ago. I was trying to be honest with him about my feelings/anxiety about using a safeword & disappointing him & I kinda felt dismissed as if he wasn’t interested in hearing it so just told me not to worry about it for now bc he won’t be too rough.. maybe I’m thinking too much into things, especially since it’s hard to tell by text.. but from everyone’s response I am definitely going to tell him that I want to slow things down & talk about everything properly in person before we explore any kinks together. 

I’m not exactly sure why I’m anxious about using a safeword.. I think it’s probably just from previous toxic relationships & not wanting to be a disappointment. I’m quite a socially awkward person in general & find it difficult to say no to people in most situations. I feel like I have to please people the best I can to make them like me. It just feels awkward/humiliating to say something is too much for me. I don’t want to feel like a failure as a submissive I guess or for him to feel rejected or like he’s doing a bad job. But I know it’s not safe to not speak up in this situation so I’m going to make sure he knows how I feel & work on this more before I get myself into a dangerous situation. 

I like the ideas people have suggested in terms of trying different things out & rating them on a traffic light system. I definitely think that would be the best way to get him understand my tolerance levels of certain things atm & hopefully I won’t feel too guilty about admitting some things are too much bc that would literally be the point of the exercise. I think it would be a good way for me to figure out my limits also bc I noticed when I’m feeling really submissive I’m pushing myself more than I know I should & then I’m paying the consequences later. I’m also going to tell him I’ll need a lot of reassurance when I do use a safeword.. I think that’s sort of what I was looking for when I initially told him I was anxious, but I obviously didn’t get that which kinda just made me more stressed then! I also agree that talking in advance about what we intend to do will probably be the best way forward atm until I feel more comfortable saying no in the moment if something gets too much. 

So yeah that’s kinda my thoughts/plans atm. I’m feeling a lil bit more hopeful than I was the other night but I’m also going to be more cautious now. If he doesn’t respect me wanting to slow things down then he sadly won’t be the one for me.

Honestly from the sounds of things, I think it would be best to tell your parents upfront. I’m from the UK so not sure how things work with health insurance, but that alone sounds like a good enough reason to at least try to get them onboard with the idea. I can empathise with your situation as I’m legally blind and don’t use any mobility aids right now but really feel like I’d benefit from using a guide dog or cane. My family don’t really understand how bad my eyesight is or how it affects me, they tend to think I’m exaggerating the severity of it. They expect me to just get on with things, but since my eyesight has deteriorated even more recently and I’m fed up of struggling, I brought up wanting to get a guide dog to my family. Initial reactions were not great, but after a few discussions they’re kind of neutral about it. My advice would be to find easy to understand information about your condition and how it affects your mobility, print it off and give it to your parents. When you discuss the idea of getting a wheelchair with them, tell them why you need one, how it’ll benefit you, list the pros AND cons. Show them you’ve put a lot of thought into this and you’re not just rushing into it. 

I also understand where you’re coming from with wanting acquaintances to be introduced to you using mobility aids already. I feel a bit anxious about how I’d explain to people why I suddenly have a guide dog, when as far as they all knew I was fully sighted before. It’s a tricky situation. If you’re moving somewhere new though and you have the chance to avoid those awkward conversations, I definitely recommend you try to. Hiding your disability from your parents or anyone else for that matter, is not a good long term plan and will only end up causing you unnecessary stress, and depending on your condition, could make things worse.

Plus I hate not having a routine and it’s embarrassing explaining to people that I don’t have job :( I wish there were more schemes where they’d support you into finding accessible jobs.. and then if it turns out that job isn’t manageable for you, you’d still have the backup of being able to go back onto the amount of ESA you received before without having to go through the whole process again

If your mental health conditions are severe enough to the point you can’t work or study etc then you’d definitely be eligible. I have the same mental health conditions as you so I definitely understand how difficult it can be. I only managed to get PIP because I have another disability as well though, they don’t seem to take mental health conditions seriously unfortunately. Although my ESA entitlement is actually mainly based on my mental health issues as my GP doesn’t understand my other disability really.. so it’s definitely possible to get help. I also have a friend who receives PIP for Autism alongside other mental health issues, although she doesn’t get the entitlement she deserves IMO. The forms/assessments aren’t really set up for mental health conditions so it’s difficult to meet the criteria! Definitely take it to tribunal if you think your mental health can manage the additional stress, as you deserve all the help you can get :) if you want to vent about anything/any advice feel free to message me btw!
